topic: Official-aligned direct `skill` tool and the free-lane description fingerprint

officialReference.skillRegistration: packages/core/src/tool/plugin/skill.ts registers `skill` with options { codemode: false }.
officialReference.wireRule: packages/core/src/tool.ts snapshot(): tools with codemode:false go on the provider's native (direct) tool list; the rest are reached through execute. Always-direct built-ins include skill, subagent, question, todo, image-generate.
officialReference.officialSkillDescription: Load a specialized skill's instructions and resources into the current conversation when the task at hand matches its description.\n\nThe skill ID must match an available skill or a skill explicitly referenced by the user.
officialReference.conclusion: The official model calls `skill` DIRECTLY (not through execute). The bridge previously declared `skill` only as a dropped Code Mode anchor, so a direct model call was discarded and the skill never loaded.

finding.summary: Declaring `skill` as a real direct tool with DSH's own description is refused by the free lane (FreeUsageLimitError, HTTP 429). The official description passes. The input schema ({name} vs official {id}) does not matter. The refusal is deterministic, not a quota/time flip.
finding.method: Same egress (direct), same model (deepseek-v4.1-flash-free), single-variable hand-built wire bodies sent over the real Bun-shaped transport, interleaved. Control = the prior anchor shape. Marker prompts only; no private conversation.

cases.name: control old anchor shape (skill as dropped anchor)
skill direct + trivial anchor description + {name} schema
skill direct + official description + official {id} schema
real DSH subagent description, direct (unchanged since 1.2.1)

finding.determinism: Two interleaved rounds: DSH-description skill -> 429 both rounds; official-description skill -> 200 both rounds. Same {name} schema, everything else identical.
finding.retryAfterCaveat: The shape refusal carries the same midnight-pointing Retry-After as a real quota exhaustion, so Retry-After alone cannot distinguish a gate refusal from quota. The interleaved same-egress control is what isolates the cause.
finding.scope: The description fingerprint was observed on the recognized `skill` name. The real (long, rich) DSH `subagent` description passes, so this is not a blanket rejection of real DSH descriptions.

fix.approach: Align with the official client: declare `skill` as a native direct tool (remove it from CODE_MODE_ANCHOR_NAMES, add it to the wire-native set beside execute/subagent), and carry the official skill description verbatim on the wire. Keep DSH's {name} input schema (also accepted) so dispatch needs no argument rewrite; skill stays out of the SDK catalog and out of execute's nested tool set, exactly like subagent.
files: src/code-mode.ts (DIRECT_SKILL_TOOL_NAME, OFFICIAL_SKILL_DESCRIPTION, anchors, instruction, nested view, renderCatalog)

endToEndVerification.realAdapterSkillCall: finish=tool-calls, dispatched call name=skill arguments={"name":"office"} (direct call round-trips to DSH dispatch).
endToEndVerification.wireDescription: skill declaration carries the official description verbatim; parameters remain DSH {name}; strict:false.
endToEndVerification.offlineSuite: 485 pass / 0 fail / 1 skipped after the change.

relationToIssue5: This makes a direct `skill` call actually load the skill (previously dropped), removing the repro obstacle where the maintainer's free-model session discarded the anchor call. It does not by itself prove the reporter's FREE_USAGE_LIMIT was quota; that still needs the reporter's diagnostic log (tool count + interleaved control). The reporter's 'my OpenCode is not exhausted' is not a valid control because the official signed-in client uses account quota while the bridge uses the egress-IP free allowance.
